metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp upward spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 2+ consecutive +1.00), model frequently under-forecasts; adjust upward by 1–3% or use sentiment-weighted median of recent 7-day window.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30-day horizon; if forecast > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 3-period EWMA of true values for 1–5 day horizon corrections.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day forecast, check sentiment history for recent reversal; if sentiment flips from -1 to +1 within 3 days, re-forecast using 14-day rolling average.
